title: RASSURE - Virtual Reality to Soothe, Secure, Simulate Uses, and Successfully Complete the Examination
official: Pilot Study Evaluating the Impact of Immersive Virtual Reality-Based Habituation to Medical Care Compared With Traditional Habituation to Medical Care on Anxiety Levels in People With Disabilities Receiving Care in a Dedicated Disability Consultation Setting
summary: The RASSURE study aims to evaluate the effect of a preparation for care programme combining a traditional habituation method with a digital immersive virtual reality tool ('PREPASOINS\_VR'), compared with traditional habituation alone. In particular, the study aims to measure the impact of the use of IVR on the anxiety experienced during the actual treatment, as well as on various indicators relating to the delivery of the treatment, its progress and the experience of the patients.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults:

  * Adults (age ≥ 18) at the time of enrollment
  * Users of the Handi Accès 35 program who have experienced treatment failure in mainstream healthcare settings
  * Individuals with a psychological or mental disability (e.g., autism spectrum disorders, Pervasive Developmental Disorder (PDD), Down syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.) that creates significant barriers to accessing care (e.g., failure to receive care, failure due to past experience (perceived/contact-related), refusal of care, architectural barriers, anticipated failure, lack of external care options) documented in the medical record
  * Requiring a period of adjustment to care
  * Having given free and informed consent
  * Able to understand the French language (care acclimatization kits-available only in French)
  * Enrolled in a social security program or eligible for an equivalent benefit

Minors:

* Children aged between 9 and 17 (inclusive) at the time of inclusion
* Users of the Handi Accès 35 scheme who have been unable to access care in mainstream settings
* People with a psychological or mental disability (for example: autism spectrum disorders, Pervasive Developmental Disorder (PDD), Down's syndrome, cerebral palsy, etc.) which creates significant barriers to accessing care (e.g. failure to access care, failure due to experience (perception/interaction), refusal of treatment, architectural barriers, anticipated failure, no external care provision) documented in the medical record
* Requiring a period of adjustment to care
* Registered with a social security scheme or entitled to an equivalent benefit
* Able to understand French (care familiarisation kits - available in French only)
* Minors for whom free, informed and written consent has been obtained from both holders of parental authority or, in exceptional cases, from a single holder under the conditions set out in Article L1122-2 of the Public Health Code.

Caregivers:

* Adult: a person aged 18 or over
* Informed consent: voluntary agreement to participate in the study following a full explanation of its terms.
* Registered with a social security scheme or an eligible dependant
* Agree to and be able to carry out the treatment familiarisation process with their relative and to accompany them to the dedicated consultation

Exclusion Criteria:

* majors : Participants requiring urgent medical care that prevents them from completing an 8-week familiarisation period with the treatment

  * Participants at high risk of epileptic seizures, or with uncontrolled epilepsy in the investigator's judgement, which contraindicates the use of VR.
  * Individuals with visual impairments that make the use of VR impossible
  * Individuals who refuse to wear the VR headset, in the investigator's judgement
  * Pregnant or breastfeeding women
  * Individuals deprived of their liberty by a judicial decision (excluding guardianship or curatorship) or an administrative decision.
  * Individuals in an emergency situation who are unable to give their prior consent.

minors : Individuals requiring urgent care that prevents them from completing an 8-week acclimatisation period

* Refusal expressed by the child, notwithstanding the prior consent of the parents or holders of parental authority
* Children subject to a court-ordered protection measure involving a specific placement, which is incompatible with participation in the study
* A person presenting a major risk of epileptic seizures, or uncontrolled epilepsy in the investigator's judgement, which contraindicates the use of VR.
* A person with visual impairments that make the use of VR impossible
* A person refusing to wear the VR headset, in the investigator's judgement
* Individuals deprived of their liberty by a judicial decision (excluding guardianship or curatorship) or an administrative decision.
* Individuals in an emergency situation who are unable to give their prior consent.

Caregiver: Vulnerable individuals referred to in Articles L. 1121-5 to 8 and L. 1122-1-2 of the Public Health Code are excluded from the study:

* Pregnant women, women in labour or breastfeeding women
* Persons deprived of their liberty by a judicial decision (including guardianship, curatorship and judicial protection) or an administrative decision
* Persons receiving psychiatric care or admitted to a health or social care facility for purposes other than research
* Persons in an emergency situation who are unable to give their prior consent
